title: A reply from the MettleUp team reaches only the phone the question was sent from
what: A member's help question carries no name or mobile number. The team's reply can be fetched only by the same phone install, using an id and a secret kept on that phone. A backup does not carry them, so after a new phone, a reinstall or a restore the member never sees replies to earlier questions, and nothing else tells them a reply came. After 30 newer questions an old one is dropped and its reply is lost too.
expected: A reply from MettleUp reaches the member wherever they use the app, for example tied to their MettleUp account when they have one, or carried in their backup.
who: members who ask for help and later change or reset their phone
how_often: every time a member changes phone or reinstalls before reading a reply
fix_line: Tie help questions to the member's account when signed in, or carry the question secrets in the backup

title: When a help message cannot be sent, the member app gives no other way to reach MettleUp
what: Help and feedback is the only way a member can reach MettleUp from the app. When both help addresses fail, the member is told to check the internet and try again, even when the help service itself is down. The app holds no MettleUp email address, phone or WhatsApp number to fall back on.
expected: When sending fails, the member is shown a working MettleUp contact (for example the support email) so a person can still be reached.
how_often: whenever the help service is down or unreachable
fix_line: Show the MettleUp support email beside the 'Couldn't send' line

title: Failures the member app catches itself never reach MettleUp
what: Crash reports cover only two cases: an error nothing caught, and a screen that crashed and showed Try again. Everything the app catches and handles quietly is only written to the phone's own log: a help message that could not be sent, a Google Play purchase that failed, a screen that shows Couldn't load, a background task that failed. MettleUp learns of these only if a member writes in, so a fault hitting many phones can stay unseen.
expected: Caught failures that stop a member's task are counted and sent to MettleUp (without personal data), so you see them before members complain.
who: you, and members hit by a silent fault
fix_line: Send a short, no-personal-data report for caught failures on key tasks, limited per run

title: The MettleUp Plus help page says gym members always get every feature free, but they lose them after their plan ends
what: The member help page says members of a gym that uses MettleUp get every feature free. The app's rule gives them the paid features only while their gym plan is open; when the owner's lock is on (the start setting), the features lock 7 days after the plan ends. A member whose plan ended is told by help that it should be free. MettleUp Plus is still switched off, so nobody sees this yet.
expected: The member help page says the features are free while the gym plan is active, and may lock some days after it ends, as the owner's help page says.
how_often: every time, once MettleUp Plus is switched on
fix_line: Change the member help page to say free while the gym plan is active

title: The member app is hard-wired to the founder's personal GitHub account and personal web address
what: Phones that installed the app from GitHub learn about new versions only by asking one GitHub account's release page, and What's new falls back to the same place. The help box and crash reports keep a backup address on the founder's personal domain, written to stay for good. These are fixed inside every installed copy: if that GitHub account is renamed, locked or lost, or the personal domain lapses, older phones silently stop hearing of updates and lose their backup help address, and only a new app version can change it. Nothing in this part of the app says who holds these accounts or how to get back in.
expected: The app's update, help and crash addresses sit on MettleUp-owned names only, with a written note of who holds each account and how to recover it.
how_often: only if the account or domain is lost, but then for every older phone
fix_line: Move update and backup addresses to MettleUp-owned names and write down who holds each account
